info.name: HRMS — Leave Salary & Offboarding
info.description:
Annual-leave salary (the accrual bucket, advance payment and encashment) plus the resignation, termination and final-settlement flows.

Spec: `leave_salary_module.xlsx` in the repo root. Legal basis: UAE Federal Decree-Law 33/2021, Art. 29 (annual leave & leave salary), Art. 43 (notice), Art. 44 (dismissal), Art. 51 (gratuity).

## Setup

1. Run **0. Auth → Login** — it stores `token` and `company_id` automatically.
2. Set `employee_id`, and `leave_type_id` / `leave_request_id` when you reach those folders.
3. Suggested first pass: flag your annual-leave type (folder 1) → dry-run the accrual (folder 2) → run it → read the summary.

## The model in four lines

- Every employee accrues annual leave monthly. Those days carry a cash value at their daily rate — `chosen base ÷ 30`.
- **The balance is derived, never stored**: `opening + accrued − taken − encashed`. Days taken come from the leave requests the company already approves, so the bucket cannot disagree with the leave module.
- **The value is revalued on read.** Art. 29 pays leave at the wage in force when it is taken, so `balance_value` uses today's rate. `booked_value` is what the days were worth when earned; the difference is the effect of pay rises.
- **The final settlement is the one snapshot.** What was agreed and paid must not move when a salary is corrected later.

## Accrual rules (UAE Art. 29)

| Service | Rate |
|---|---|
| below 6 months | nothing accrues (booked as deferred rows) |
| 6 – 12 months | 2 days/month, and the deferred months are credited retrospectively |
| 12 months + | 2.5 days/month, applied to the whole first year too |

So an employee at 11 months holds 22 days, and one who has just completed a year holds the statutory 30 — the step-up shows on the ledger as `catch_up_days` rather than being folded silently into the rate.

## Watch for

- **Flag your annual-leave type first.** Until one carries `counts_toward_leave_salary`, leave taken never draws the balance down.
- The daily rate is carried at **4 decimals** (`NUMERIC(12,4)`) and only the final amount is rounded. 8,000/30 rounded to 266.67 first turns a 20-day advance into 5,333.40 instead of 5,333.33.
- Money from the calculation endpoints is JSON **numbers**; money read straight off a table comes back as **strings** (node-pg NUMERIC). Both appear in these examples.
- The unpaid-leave deduction endpoint is **indicative only** — payroll generation applies the real one. Never render it as payable.
- Nothing deactivates an employee until a separation is **completed**.

Not legal advice — verify the statutory figures against your jurisdiction and contracts before go-live.

item.name: 1b. Going Live — opening balances
item.description:
How a company that has been running for years starts using the module.

One **cutoff date** (their go-live) plus a day count per employee. Accrual is then only booked for months completing after that date, so the imported figure and the ledger cannot cover the same month twice.

The import is **all-or-nothing** — one bad row rejects the batch and writes nothing.

item.name: 2. The Bucket — balances & accrual
item.description:
The balance is DERIVED on every read: `opening + accrued − taken − encashed`. There is no balance column.

`balance_value` is the balance revalued at TODAY's daily rate (what Art. 29 entitles the employee to). `booked_value` is what those days were worth when they were earned. The gap between them is the effect of pay rises — surface `revaluation_difference` on finance screens, not on the employee's.

item.name: Rebuild after changing an accrual rule

request.description:
Run this after changing min_service_months, full_service_months or either rate — the settings save returns a warning telling you so.

`recalculate` rebuilds the DAY COUNTS under the current rules and **keeps each month's original rate snapshot** (a rule change did not alter what a day was worth in March).

Without it, lowering the eligibility threshold from 6 to 5 leaves an affected employee on 4 days where they should hold 14 — the catch-up belongs to a month already on the ledger as a zero, and a normal run never revisits it.

`pending → approved → completed`, with `rejected`, `withdrawn` and `cancelled` as terminal exits.

item.name: 8. Final Settlement
item.description:
The preview is computed live and writes nothing. Saving FREEZES it — unlike balances and gratuity, which are derived on every read everywhere else, what was agreed and paid must not move when a salary is corrected next month.

Saving also raises the encashment that pays the balance out, which is what removes those days from the bucket.

Gated by `offboarding.settlement`.
